rules.quote: Only use mathematical symbols in general content if user research shows they are appropriate for your users and for the type of content.
rules.specification: Symbols are not intrinsically violations. A finding requires knowing whether supporting user research exists; that cannot generally be established from the text alone.

rules.why: G-2 combines the audience and research conditions; G-3 preserves supported symbol use as an exception; G-4 consolidates repeated wording. E-2 assigns the range and balance contrasts to the words rule they actually test.

rules.specification: The page gives no fixed list of unfamiliar terminology or required level of explanation. Audience familiarity and adequacy of an explanation require editorial judgement.

when: Mathematical terminology or concepts need explanation for the intended users.
rules.why: G-5 excludes the reminder to the writer, but the required plain-language explanation is a property of the text.

rules.quote: Use code, not punctuation, for mathematical symbols
rules.specification: Judge the resulting characters, not the input method. The table gives conflicting Unicode values for ≠ and >, so those table entries need review before implementation. Valid mathematical alternatives such as the dot operator, asterisk and division slash are governed by the separate usage rules, rather than automatically treated as encoding errors.
rules.violation_condition: Mathematical notation contains an incorrectly encoded substitute, such as a hyphen or dash for minus, the letter x for multiplication, or >= and <= for mathematical relations.
when: Applies when mathematical symbols are used.

The prose identifies − as U+2212, × as U+00D7, ÷ as U+00F7 and ∕ as U+2215.

rules.why: G-2 combines character-substitution cases and G-4 absorbs the repeated minus, multiplication and relation instructions. The valid-alternative preferences remain separate because they are not encoding failures.
